subject: Human Evolution
title: Arboreal Origins
description: Learn Arboreal Origins in one minute.

hook.text: Orangutans walk upright on branches, steadying themselves with their arms. Sound familiar?

buildup.text: Some researchers think bipedalism started in the trees, not on the ground—standing to reach fruit.

discovery.text: Upright posture on flexible branches improves balance and extends reach, a clear feeding advantage.

twist.text: If true, bipedalism was an arboreal skill that transferred to the ground—not a grassland invention.

climax.text: Ardi's grasping feet support this: she walked upright but still spent time in trees 4.4 million years ago.

punchline.text: We may have walked upright on branches first.

quiz.question: What supports the arboreal origin of bipedalism?
options: Orangutans walk upright on branches; Ardi had grasping feet
